annotations.title: Heritage designations at a place in Flanders (Onroerend Erfgoed)

description: Whether an address or point in Flanders is protected or listed heritage, and what that means for works and permits, from the Flemish heritage agency (Onroerend Erfgoed) via the public Mercator map service. Checks every legal designation at the point: protected monument, protected town or village view, protected landscape, protected archaeological site, transition zone, UNESCO core or buffer zone, fixed inventory of built or landscape heritage, fixed archaeological zone (archaeology note needed for smaller works), heritage landscape and area where no archaeology is expected (no archaeology note needed). Each comes with its name, id, date, the official decision link and what it means. Also the scientific inventory of built heritage (no legal effect), ratified archaeology notes at the point, protected monuments within 30 m, and the municipality (NIS code). Flanders only. Starts with key_facts. Checks one point, not a whole parcel; does not replace the permit procedure or give zoning (spatial plans). Examples: Is the building on Bruges' Markt protected heritage? → {"address":"Markt 1, 8000 Brugge"}; Is Leuven station a protected monument? → {"address":"Martelarenplein 20, 3000 Leuven"}; Which heritage rules apply at this point in Antwerp? → {"latitude":51.2194,"longitude":4.4025}.

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude, e.g. 51.0453 (use with longitude instead of address).

x_lambert72.description: Belgian Lambert 72 (EPSG:31370) x in metres, as an alternative to latitude/longitude.
